prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for every homeowner — the right one depends on your budget, the type of roof and materials you want, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and the contractor’s track record for workmanship and service. I can help you find one, but here are practical steps and what to look for so you pick the best Dallas contractor for your roof replacement.

Quick checklist to find a great roofer
- Local reputation: 4+ star reviews on Google/Yelp/Angi, plus positive recent references.  
- Proper insurance: ask for current general liability and workers’ comp certificates naming you as an additional insured while work is in progress (or confirm coverage).  
- Licenses/registrations: Texas does not have a statewide roofing license, but check city registration/permits (City of Dallas requirements) and any local trade registrations.  
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, etc. — indicates training and eligibility for extended warranties.  
- Written estimate and contract: scope of work, materials/brands, tear-off vs layover, number of roofing layers, ventilation, flashing, disposal, start/completion dates, payment schedule, and warranty details.  
- Warranties: manufacturer (shingles) and workmanship (ask how long and if it’s transferable). Get warranties in writing.  
- Insurance-claim experience: if filing with your homeowner insurer, pick a contractor familiar with claims and scope documentation.  
- Local references and photos of finished jobs (preferably recent storm jobs, if relevant).  
- No high-pressure sales: avoid door-to-door storm chasers or urgent “act now” pressure.

Red flags
- No proof of insurance or refuse to provide certificates.  
- Requires large upfront cash payment (avoid paying full amount up front).  
- Vague contract or refuses to put details in writing.  
- Extremely low bids with push to sign immediately.  
- No local address or only P.O. box; cannot provide references.

Questions to ask each company
- How long have you been in business in Dallas?  
- Are you licensed/registered with the City of Dallas (if required) and can you pull permits?  
- Can you provide references and photos of recent complete replacements?  
- Which shingle brands and underlayments do you use? Are you a certified installer for them?  
- What are the warranties (manufacturer and workmanship) and what do they cover?  
- How many layers will be removed and how will you handle ventilation and flashing?  
- What is the payment schedule and final cleanup process (including nails)?  
- Will you provide a written contract and proof of insurance?

How to get reliable bids
- Get at least 3 written estimates with the same scope.  
- Compare materials, number of tear-off layers, ventilation upgrades, storm-damage repairs, and warranties (don’t just compare price).  
- Ask to see a copy of their insurance certificate and a lien waiver for final payment.

Where to look for candidates
- Google and Yelp (look at recent reviews).  
- Angi/HomeAdvisor for vetted contractors.  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) for complaints history.  
- Local Facebook groups or Nextdoor for neighborhood referrals.  
- Ask your insurance agent for preferred contractors they’ve worked with.

If you want, I can:
- Find and shortlist well-reviewed Dallas roofers (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood).  
- Provide a sample contract checklist you can give to contractors.  
- Help evaluate estimates you receive (paste or summarize them).

Which of those would you like me to do next?
